title: Private Network Change Review Runbook (draft)
content:
Status: draft

Overview
This runbook describes the proposed Network Change Review (NCR) pipeline for Private deployments where customers manage portions of their network (VPC peering, static routes, NAT/egress, firewall rules). Purpose: provide a lightweight, auditable, and automatable flow that gates customer-requested networking changes through product and security checks, collects evidence for compliance, and emits machine‑readable audit logs suitable for customer export and internal incident forensics.

Why this exists (Problem statement)
- Customers frequently request network configuration changes tied to private deployments (e.g., add route for on-prem connectivity, open port for monitoring).
- Current ad hoc Slack/email approvals create noisy, inconsistent audit records and slow down onboarding.
- We need an interoperable pattern that supports: human approvals, policy-as-code enforcement, and a canonical audit artifact that customers and auditors can consume.

Goals
- Define a single NCR pipeline that covers: request intake, automated policy checks, approver selection, evidence bundling, approval/denial, and immutable audit emission.
- Produce an audit artifact schema (JSON lines) that can be shipped to customer SIEM or Redwood Console retention.
- Allow customer-managed network changes to be executed by operators or automatically when safe, with clear escalation paths.

Non‑Goals
- This doc does not rework the entire on-prem installer.
- Not covering low-level OS firewall tuning; focus is on cloud networking abstractions (routes, peering, security groups, NAT).

User stories
- As an IT admin at Customer X, I want a clear approval trail when Redwood requests a new route be added so I can satisfy my auditor.
- As an SRE, I want automated prechecks (reachable endpoints, overlapping CIDRs) so I don’t approve destructive changes by accident.
- As Product Security, I want policy violations bubbled up with remediation suggestions.

High-level flow
1) Request creation: change request created via Console or ticket template. Minimal required fields: customer_id, deployment_id, requester, change_type, diff (before/after), justification, desired_window.
2) Automated prechecks: run static checks (CIDR overlap, blacklisted ports), dynamic checks (ping/port probe via staging path), configuration drift check. Any failed check attaches "precheck_failure" metadata and blocks auto-approve.
3) Policy-as-code evaluation: evaluate against active rules (e.g., allowed port ranges, mandated egress inspection). Rules can be maintained in repo (policy repo) and versioned; evaluation produces a rule set hash for traceability.
4) Approver selection: deterministic approver list determined by customer config (customer approver pool or Redwood delegations). For delegated approvals, include delegated_admin_id and link to delegation record.
5) Approval gating: one of these outcomes — auto-approved, requires single approver, requires 2-step (security+ops), denied. Approvals must include typed reason and optional evidence attachment (pcap, traceroute, screenshots).
6) Execution: operator executes change or system applies it for safe, auto-approved changes. Every action recorded with actor_id and execution transcript.
7) Audit emission: on finalization, emit a canonical audit entry (see schema below), store immutable copy in deployment bucket and forward to configured sinks.

Audit artifact schema (summary)
Each finalized NCR must produce a single JSON line document (newline-delimited JSON) with the following top-level fields:
- id: unique UUIDv4 for the change request
- customer_id
- deployment_id
- created_at, closed_at (ISO8601)
- requester_id, approver_ids (array)
- change_type (route_add|route_delete|peering|nat_update|security_group)
- diff: short text or structured array describing before/after
- policy_evaluation: pass|fail|warning and rule_hash (git commit or version)
- prechecks: array of {name, status, message}
- evidence_urls: array of stable URLs to attachments (S3/gs links)
- execution_log_url: link to operator transcript
- final_status: approved|denied|cancelled|failed
- signatures: array of {actor_id, timestamp, signature_type} (optional; for enterprise legal signoffs)
- retention_policy: id linking to retention configuration

Note: sample JSONs are attached as a separate technical appendix (TBD). Keep schema minimal to make forwarding to SIEMs simple.

Approval gates and timing
- Safety gate: prechecks + policy_pass required for any auto-apply.
- Security gate: if change_type touches egress or firewall, require security approver unless the customer maintains an explicit waiver.
- High-risk timing: disallow auto-apply in production windows defined by customer (e.g., 08:00-18:00 business) unless explicit override with 2 approvers.
- Escalation: If approver does not respond in 24h, escalate to on-call and notify customer primary. For high‑risk requests, escalate after 4h.

Implementation considerations
- Policy repo: store Rego or Open Policy Agent rules in infra repo; every evaluation returns rule_hash used in audit.
- Precheck runners: containerized jobs run inside dedicated sandbox network with ephemeral credentials; results are deterministic and recorded.
- Delegated approvals: model delegation object with expiry and scope (resource types, CIDR ranges) — audit records must include delegation_id.
- Immutable storage: write finalized audit lines to WORM-enabled bucket with server-side encryption and object immutability flags where supported.
- Export connectors: provide export adapters (S3, GCS, syslog->SIEM) with configurable filters and retention overlays.

Security and compliance notes
- Avoid embedding raw secrets or credentials in evidence artifacts; scan uploads and mask tokens before retention.
- Support customer KMS for encrypting audit stores in Private deployments.
- Maintain retention metadata to support legal hold requests.

Operational runbook snippets (for operators)
- Quick validate: run `ncr validate <request-id>` which fetches request, replays prechecks, and prints policy diff.
- Force apply: only for emergency with 2 approvers and documented rollback plan; record `force_reason` and require post-mortem.
- Rollback pattern: capture pre-change snapshot (route table, firewall rules) and provide `ncr rollback <id>` which uses snapshot to restore.

Customer UX notes (Console)
- Streamlined request form with recommended fields and inline precheck results.
- Preview of audit artifact prior to submission with hash for customer records.
- In customer-managed networks, provide step-by-step change instructions so customers can run changes themselves and upload evidence (preferred for high-security customers).

Rollout plan
- Phase 0 (pilot): implement pipeline for internal staging deployments and 2 pilot customers — target 6 weeks.
- Phase 1: enable for all new private deployments as opt-in, collect feedback and measure approval latency and precheck failure rate (2 months).
- Phase 2: require for select network change classes and open-source policy rules to customers.

Telemetry and KPIs
- Avg time from request -> first decision
- % of requests auto-approved
- Precheck failure categories and top-5 rules causing blocks
- Number of escalations and emergency force-applies
- Audit export success rate and retention compliance checks

Open questions / decisions needed
- Should we require cryptographic signatures for approvers in enterprise plans? (legal vs friction tradeoff)
- Default retention: 365 days or align with customer-specified retention by default?
- Which approval UI should be primary: Console or email action links?

Next steps
- Align with Security on rule set and escalation SLA (owners: Miguel Rivera, Roshni Patel).
- Prototype precheck runner and a sample audit line emitter (owner: Ava Chen).
- Create a short pilot checklist and identify two customers for pilot (due: 2024-12-06).

Notes and references
- See linked Confluence page for current policy drafts.
- Related Jira: ENG-1342 (policy repo work), SRE-287 (operator CLI).

Author notes (Priya): this is intentionally lightweight and focused on the artifact shape and gating flow. Need design review with SRE and Security before moving to engineering tickets.
